Sara — quick readout and recommended next steps (attached CSV and MAP):

Key findings (Hosted environment):
- Performance: rw-3B-quant delivers the best latency profile and scales to high concurrency with minimal TTFT impact (p50 48ms @1, p50 180ms @16). Ideal for user-facing pathways requiring sub-250ms median.
- Throughput: rw-3B sustained throughput highest per cost (650 req/s @16 concurrency).
- Quality: rw-3B automated pass 87%; edge cases missed in ~13% (examples in variant_quality_notes.md).

- rw-7B-fp16 is a middle ground (better quality at ~94% pass, moderate latency).
- rw-13B-qtz shows the best quality for sensitive summarization (97% pass) but exhibits large p95 and OOM risk at high concurrency — more suited to batch/async workflows or Dedicated pools with larger memory profiles.

Recommendation for Greenvale initial rollout:
- Primary: rw-3B-quant on Redwood Hosted for the patient-facing quick-reply flow (low latency imperative).
- Secondary: rw-7B-fp16 for clinician-facing summaries where quality tolerance is higher.
- Offload heavy summarization to rw-13B-qtz in Dedicated capacity (scheduled jobs) to avoid p95 hits on real-time latency SLOs.

Close timeline:
- Dec 2: Redwood to submit final SOW (we will include a Dedicated config option and fallback policies)
- Dec 4: Greenvale review & procurement redlines
- Dec 8–10: Signatures & initial reserved capacity provisioning

Please confirm: does the Greenvale exec team want us to prepare a cost comparison (per 1M tokens + Dedicated monthly commit) for the three-path recommendation? Rafael and I can produce that by Dec 3 if helpful.

Thanks — great progress.
